_comment_purpose: Vocab overlay for --mode data-first (issue #278). Merged on top of templates/agents/finance/vocab.json by setup.sh; only fields whose meaning changes under data-first appear here. Fields not listed inherit from the base finance vocab. The genre: the paper's primary contribution is an open, documented, validated dataset plus a portfolio of facts established on it (Chen & Zimmermann RevFin 2022; Jensen-Kelly-Pedersen JF 2023; Welch & Goyal RFS 2008; Hoberg & Phillips RFS 2010/JPE 2016; Baker-Bloom-Davis QJE 2016).
_comment_theory_generator: Dataset-spec mode reframes theory-generator as a data-architecture writer, not a theorem prover. The body lives at templates/agent_bodies/shared_modes/data_first/theory-generator-core.md.
THEORY_GEN_ROLE: finance researcher writing the data-architecture specification of a data-contribution paper
THEORY_GEN_DESCRIPTION: Writes the dataset specification of a data-contribution finance paper. The orchestrator launches this agent at Stage 2 (Dataset Specification). Reads the selected architecture sketch, the Stage 1 pilot-build report, and the Stage 3a construction results when present; produces a full data-architecture document — per-source provenance, schema, dating/timestamp conventions, inclusion rules, cross-source reconciliation rules, redistribution-rights inventory, validation plan, and fact-portfolio plan — not a theorem-and-proof structural model. Supports fresh, mutate, crossover, and pivot strategies based on attempt history.
_comment_idea_prototyper: Dataset mode reframes idea-prototyper from a theorem-feasibility checker to a pilot builder. The body lives at templates/agent_bodies/shared_modes/data_first/idea-prototyper.md and pulls a real slice from each named source to verify access, format, and claimed coverage (consumed by dataset-spec-mode theory-generator at Stage 2). The TRACTABLE / BLOCKED-DIFFICULTY / BLOCKED-IMPOSSIBLE verdict stays shape-compatible with the existing stage_1.md Step 2 / Step 3 flow (an inaccessible or redistribution-restricted core source is IMPOSSIBLE for an open dataset; a brittle-but-workable access path is DIFFICULTY).
IDEA_PROTOTYPER_DESCRIPTION: Pilot build of a selected dataset architecture. Launched between architecture selection and the Stage 2 dataset specification to verify each named source is accessible, parseable, and actually carries the coverage the sketch claims — by pulling a real slice, not by reading documentation. If a core source is inaccessible or redistribution-restricted the architecture is killed; a mere access-path difficulty (a scrape where an API was hoped for) survives to Stage 2.
_comment_idea_reviewer: idea-reviewer's tractability and importance gut-checks recalibrate for data papers: tractability is about source accessibility, redistribution rights, and reconciliation feasibility; importance is about demand — how many papers would have used this dataset — plus the substantive edge (adjudications and new facts) that separates top-3 from field-tier data papers.
IDEA_TRACTABILITY_BULLETS:
- Is every core source accessible to this project (public download, free API, or an already-credentialed subscription)? An architecture whose backbone source cannot be pulled is dead at Stage 1.
- Can the assembled dataset be released openly? Government and self-published sources usually clear; licensed databases (WRDS-derived extracts, commercial feeds) generally cannot be redistributed — a core source that forces the release to be build-from-source-only is a difficulty; one that blocks any open release is fatal.
- Do the sources share (or map onto) a common identifier and time convention, or is the reconciliation itself a research project? A dataset whose event classes cannot be dated on a common timeline fails at the join.
- Is there a second independent source for each major event class, so coverage can be triangulated? A single-sourced dataset cannot support the validation section a referee will demand.
- Is the assembly repeatable by code alone? Hand-curation steps that cannot be scripted make the build non-reproducible and the release claim hollow.
IDEA_IMPORTANCE_BULLETS:
- How many published papers hand-collected some version of this data? Count them — that count is the demand evidence. A dataset nobody has ever needed to hand-collect is a dataset nobody needs.
- Does the dataset let the paper adjudicate at least one published disagreement that plausibly traces to data construction (different dating conventions, different vintages, different inclusion rules)? Adjudication is the substantive edge that separates a top-3 data paper from a field-tier one.
- Does it enable a fact class that existing data cannot support (a finer timestamp, a longer panel, a unified cross-source view)?
- Would a seminar audience use it next week, or admire it and move on? Infrastructure that changes what the field can measure is important; a tidier copy of accessible data is not.
THEORY_PARSIMONY_THRESHOLD: an event class or construction convention that no fact in the portfolio consumes
THEORY_WEAKEST_POINT_LIST: ambiguous inclusion rule, undocumented dating convention, single-sourced event class with no triangulation path, redistribution right asserted but not verified, or a fact portfolio the schema cannot actually support
THEORY_SANITY_EXAMPLE_BAD: claiming complete coverage of unscheduled FOMC actions from a source that only archives scheduled meetings
_comment_mechanism_term: Data papers have no economic mechanism to defend; the analogous load-bearing object is the construction — the set of choices (sources, dating, inclusion, reconciliation) that produce the dataset and could manufacture or destroy a documented fact. The MECHANISM_TERM_* keys carry that change into referee, self-attacker, and other agents whose bodies use them.
_comment_referee: referee-core.md drives the structured top-3 finance referee. The data-first referee evaluates a data-contribution paper: the dataset is the deliverable and the facts section is its demonstration, so validation credibility and demand replace identification credibility and theorem depth.
REFEREE_JOURNAL_ROLE: **top-3 finance journal** (JF, JFE, RFS), evaluating a data-contribution paper whose deliverable is an open, documented, validated dataset plus a portfolio of documented facts (no structural model, no primary causal claim)
REFEREE_MIDDLE_BULLETS:
- **Is the construction trustworthy?** Are inclusion rules stated precisely enough that a third party could rebuild the dataset from the named sources and get the same rows? Are dating/timestamp conventions (timezone, vintage, revision policy) explicit? Is every major event class triangulated against a second independent source, with discrepancies reconciled in writing? Construction opacity is the first reason to reject a data paper at a top-3 finance journal.
- **Does the validation section actually validate?** Do the known results the paper replicates (announcement premia, pre-event drift, seasonalities — whatever the portfolio claims) reproduce on the new data with the documented sign and magnitude? Where a replication fails, does the paper trace the failure to a construction difference, or wave it away?
- **Are the facts robust to construction choices?** For each headline fact, would the natural alternative convention (a different dating rule, a different dedup rule, a different vintage policy) preserve it? A fact that exists only under the paper's specific construction is an artifact until proven otherwise.
- **Is the incumbent comparison honest?** What existing datasets cover parts of this ground, and does the paper state precisely what they lack? Overlap understated is the data-paper equivalent of a buried literature review.
- **Is the release real?** Versioned data (or build-from-source code where redistribution is restricted), documented schema, runnable build code. A data paper whose data cannot actually be obtained is vaporware.
REFEREE_FINAL_BULLET: Does it pass the "who builds on this" test? — will other researchers use this dataset next year, or is it a tidier copy of what they already have?
_comment_scorer_h3: Hard requirement H3 swaps from 'math audit passed' (irrelevant under dataset-spec mode where the math audits never fire) to the construction/validation audit chain that gates a data paper's correctness: empirics audit + data-integrity audit + data-selection audit + coverage audit, with headline replication PASS and a fresh spec audit. There is no theorem backstop — a wrong row count, silent sample exclusion, or untriangulated event class ships unless these gates catch it. H1, H2, H4, H5 carry over.
H3_REQUIREMENT: Empirics audit, both data audits (integrity + selection), and the coverage audit passed; headline replication PASS; spec audit fresh
H3_CHECK: empirics-auditor returned PASS on the executed build and analysis code, data-integrity-auditor and data-selection-auditor returned PASS on the cached datasets (Stage 3a step 7.5), coverage-auditor returned PASS on the triangulation protocol (every event class cross-checked against a second independent source, every discrepancy reconciled in writing), headline-replicator PASS covers the headline facts and coverage counts, AND `pipeline_state.json:dataset_spec_version == theory_version` (a stale spec audit is a hard block, mirroring the empirical-first mechanism-staleness rule). None of the gates may have been bypassed or treated as a soft check — each must show an explicit PASS verdict in its audit file.
H3_FAIL_ROUTING: REVISE — re-fire the failing auditor's REVISE/FAIL loop per `docs/stage_3a_empirical.md`. If empirics-auditor failed: empiricist must fix the named code/methodology issues within the 5-attempt cap. If either data auditor failed: route per step 7.5 — REVISE re-launches the empiricist on the named failure modes within the 3-round cap (loops.data_integrity.round); FAIL is a hard escalation (cache fundamentally unreliable), re-execute the data layer before re-entering scoring. If coverage-auditor failed: route per the coverage-audit step — REVISE re-launches the empiricist on the named event classes within the 3-round cap (loops.coverage_audit.round); FAIL means an event class is untriangulable as scoped, return to Stage 2 to rescope or waive it explicitly in the spec. If the spec audit is stale: re-run the Stage 2 spec audit on the revised spec before proceeding.
H3_OUTPUT_LABEL: Empirics + data-integrity + data-selection + coverage audits passed, headline replication PASS, spec audit fresh
H3_BRIEF: Stage 3a construction/validation chain — empirics, both data audits, coverage triangulation, headline replication, spec freshness
_comment_scorer_calibrations: Rigor / Novelty / Surprise calibrations re-anchor from theorem properties to data-paper properties (provenance + triangulated coverage + replication; incumbent-relative novelty with an explicit two-tier split; usefulness and new-fact surprise). Importance, Parsimony, Fertility carry over from base finance vocab because their criteria are mode-invariant.
RIGOR_100: full provenance chain (every field traceable to a named source query with date and version), every event class triangulated against ≥2 independent sources with a written per-discrepancy reconciliation log, every headline fact independently replicated from raw sources, explicit dating/timezone/vintage conventions with sensitivity checks on the natural alternatives, AND clean audits across the chain (empirics, data-integrity, data-selection, coverage all PASS with zero severity-5+ findings). Coverage-auditor PASS without REVISE rounds.
RIGOR_80: full provenance and triangulation with minor gaps documented and waived explicitly in the spec (e.g., one peripheral event class single-sourced with a stated reason), sound build code, replications of the portfolio's known facts, AND the full audit chain PASS. **Default for data papers that pass all Stage 3a audits (empirics, data-integrity, data-selection, coverage).** The number of REVISE rounds an audit needed is a process signal, not a quality signal on the final paper. Score below 80 only if reader-noticeable construction ambiguities or unreconciled discrepancies remain despite audit passage.
RIGOR_60: construction is documented but validation is thin (e.g., triangulation run on some event classes but not others without a stated waiver, replications qualitative rather than quantitative, dating conventions stated but never stress-tested against alternatives). The paper would survive a first read but not a referee who tries to rebuild one event class.
NOVELTY_CALIBRATION: explicitly two-tier — do not pretend infrastructure alone clears the top-3 bar: a dataset that fills a genuinely open gap AND adjudicates a published disagreement or documents a genuinely new fact = 100; a dataset that fills a genuinely open gap with replications and incremental facts only (infrastructure value alone) = 70, and honest routing for this profile is the field tier (Review of Finance / JFQA band — the Chen-Zimmermann precedent), not JF/JFE/RFS; a unified/cleaned version of data that is already open in scattered form, with no new fact = 40; a re-release of an existing dataset with cosmetic additions = 15
SURPRISE_CALIBRATION: a documented fact that overturns a published result and traces the disagreement to a specific construction difference in the prior data = 85-100; a genuinely new fact the field could not have called ex-ante, established on the new data = 75; a known fact whose magnitude or timing shifts materially on the corrected data = 60; replications that confirm known facts with better data = 40 (this is the validation section doing its job, not a surprise); a tidier estimate of an uncontested number = 15
_comment_answer_symmetry: Stage-0 answer-symmetry (#132) was authored for theory-first, where the contribution is a headline prediction that must survive its own null. Data-first replaces answer-symmetry with value-symmetry: the deliverable is the dataset, so a fact portfolio that comes back null is still a contribution provided the infrastructure demand is real — but a null-portfolio dataset is field-tier, and the question-referee must say so rather than bless top-3 framing on infrastructure value alone.
QUESTION_POSER_DEAD_BRANCH: Flag — but do not automatically abandon — any answer that would be a non-paper. In this data-first pipeline the contribution is the **dataset**, so value-symmetry replaces answer-symmetry: the question is live even if every candidate new fact comes back null, *provided the demand evidence is real* (papers that hand-collect this data exist and are named). State the tier consequence honestly: a dataset whose portfolio is adjudication-free and null is field-tier infrastructure, not a top-3 paper. The dead branch is a dataset with no demand evidence — no paper has ever needed this data — which is a gap-selection failure to send back, never a reason to inflate the fact portfolio here.
QUESTION_REFEREE_DEAD_BRANCH:
- Enumerate the plausible outcomes of the fact portfolio. In this data-first pipeline the contribution is the **dataset**, so a null portfolio is a **live** branch on its own terms — value-symmetry, not answer-symmetry — *provided the demand evidence is real* (published papers that hand-collected some version of this data are named and counted).
- Apply the two-tier consequence honestly: dataset + adjudication of a published disagreement (or a genuinely new fact) supports top-3 framing; dataset + replications only is field-tier infrastructure. REVISE a question posed at top-3 on infrastructure value alone.
- The only dead branch is a dataset with no demand evidence — nobody has ever hand-collected it, no named paper would have used it. That is a **gap-selection failure** (it should have been caught at Step 0b), so the REVISE fix is to re-pose toward data the field demonstrably needs — not to manufacture a speculative fact portfolio.
_comment_empirics_auditor: empirics-auditor (extension agent) gets a dataset-construction-fitness gate added under data-first mode. The default vocab leaves EMPIRICS_AUDITOR_MODE_BLOCK empty so theory-first --ext empirical deploys keep the existing audit scope. Under data-first, the block adds explicit checks that the built dataset implements the Stage 2 spec — a build that runs and passes code checks can still silently deviate from the spec it claims to implement.
EMPIRICS_AUDITOR_MODE_BLOCK:
### Spec conformance of the built dataset (data-first mode)

The Stage 2 spec audit verified that the **specification** is coherent. Your job here is to verify that the **built dataset** implements that specification — a build that runs, matches its own report, and passes the code checks above can still deviate silently from the spec.

Read `output/stage2/theory_draft_v{theory_version}.md` (the binding dataset specification) before running these checks.

- **Schema conformance:** does the built dataset's schema (columns, types, keys, one-row-per-what) match the spec's schema section exactly? Any column added, dropped, or re-typed without a spec revision is a flag.
- **Inclusion rules as implemented:** re-read each inclusion rule in the spec and find the exact code that implements it. A rule stated in the spec but enforced nowhere in code — or a filter in code that no spec rule licenses — is a flag.
- **Dating conventions as implemented:** the spec commits to timestamp conventions (timezone, exact-time vs date-only, vintage policy, revision handling). Verify the build code actually applies them: check a sample of rows for each event class against the convention, not just the code path.
- **Reconciliation rules as implemented:** where the spec defines how conflicting sources are reconciled (priority order, tolerance windows, manual-override log), verify the implementation matches and that every manual override is logged with a reason.
- **Redistribution boundary respected:** verify no field from a redistribution-restricted source appears in the release artifact under `output/dataset/` — restricted inputs may feed build-from-source code only. This is a hard flag, not a style note.
- **Coverage counts reproduce:** the headline coverage counts (events per class per period) that the paper reports must reproduce from the shipped build code on the cached inputs. Recompute them; do not trust the report.

These conformance checks are independent of the data/code/statistical checks above. A dataset can be correctly cached and cleanly coded and still fail conformance because it quietly implements a different spec than the one the paper documents.
_comment_self_attacker: self-attacker-core.md attack vectors get re-targeted from theorems-and-mechanisms to construction-and-facts. Equilibrium and macro sections stay empty (theory-only constructs). Importance, completeness, and literature framings carry over with data-paper-flavored examples.
SELF_ATTACK_RESULT_BULLETS:
- Is any headline fact an artifact of a construction choice? Rerun it under the natural alternative convention (a different dating rule, dedup rule, vintage policy, or reconciliation priority) and see if it survives.
- Is any coverage claim quietly single-sourced? An event class triangulated against a mirror of the same underlying source is not triangulated at all.
- Does any dated event carry look-ahead — a timestamp only knowable after the fact (a revised release time, a backfilled announcement), used as if it were known in real time?
- Do the coverage counts hide survivorship — a source archive that silently drops cancelled, rescheduled, or superseded events, making the calendar look cleaner than history was?
SELF_ATTACK_MECHANISM_BULLETS:
- Does the reconciliation rule manufacture facts? A priority order that always prefers the source with the earlier timestamp will mechanically create 'pre-event drift' relative to papers that used the later stamp. Check each headline fact against the reconciliation choices it depends on.
- Are timezone and daylight-saving conventions consistent across sources and decades? A one-hour misalignment turns same-day into next-day for late-afternoon events and silently corrupts every intraday fact.
- Is any deduplication rule deleting real events? Two genuine events close in time (an unscheduled meeting the day before a scheduled one) look exactly like a duplicate to a naive window rule.
- Does vintage confusion contaminate the panel — current-vintage values attached to historical dates where the spec promised as-known-at-the-time values?
SELF_ATTACK_COMPLETENESS_BULLETS:
- What event class would a referee expect this dataset to cover that it silently omits? An 'FOMC calendar' without unscheduled actions, or a 'macro release calendar' without revision announcements, invites the first question of the seminar.
- What does the closest incumbent dataset have that this one lacks? Understating incumbent overlap is the fastest route to a rejection letter from a referee who built the incumbent.
- Which replication target in the fact portfolio was NOT run, and why? An unrun replication reads as a failed one.
- What sample-period boundary is load-bearing? Facts documented on a period chosen after looking at the data are curve-fit until shown robust to the natural alternative windows.
SELF_ATTACK_TARGET_EXAMPLE: the claim that scheduled-announcement coverage is complete before 1994, when the primary source's archive only begins reliably in 1994 (Stage 2 spec, coverage section)
SELF_ATTACK_RULE_EXAMPLE: The pre-announcement drift fact is measured against the reconciled timestamp, but the reconciliation rule prefers the earlier of two source timestamps — so the documented 'drift' window mechanically contains part of the announcement itself under the alternative stamp, and the fact may not survive the other convention
